theme: सांख्य-ज्ञान और कर्मयोग एक ही लक्ष्य की दो दृष्टियाँ हैं। / Knowledge and action are two expressions of the same liberation.
context: Arjuna is comparing renunciation and active discipline. Krishna answers that the destination is the same: liberation from egoic bondage. The real issue is not whether one acts or withdraws, but whether one acts without attachment and sees the Self in all beings.
contextHindi: अर्जुन संन्यास और कर्मयोग में कौन-सी मार्ग श्रेष्ठ है, इसका विचार कर रहे हैं। कृष्ण कहते हैं कि लक्ष्य एक है: अहंकार से मुक्ति। असली सवाल यह नहीं है कि कोई काम करे या न करे, बल्कि वह बिना आसक्ति के, आत्म-बोध के साथ करे या नहीं।
sanskritDevanagari:
यत्साङ्ख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते |
एकं साङ्ख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति ||५-५||
transliteration:
yatsāṅkhyaiḥ prāpyate sthānaṃ tadyogairapi gamyate .
ekaṃ sāṅkhyaṃ ca yogaṃ ca yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati ||5-5||

wordByWord.meaning: that which; the state or goal
by those who pursue knowledge or discernment; by jñāna-oriented seekers
by yogis; by those practising disciplined action

spokenHindi: यह श्लोक बहुत साफ़ बताता है कि ज्ञान-मार्ग और कर्म-मार्ग, अगर सही अर्थ में समझे जाएँ, तो अपने लक्ष्य में एक ही हैं। कृष्ण कहते हैं कि जिस स्थान को ‘सांख्य’ के मार्ग से व्यक्ति प्राप्त करता है, उसी स्थान को योग का साधक भी प्राप्त करता है। यहाँ ‘सांख्य’ का अर्थ सिर्फ़ तत्त्व-अवधारणा नहीं है; इसका अर्थ है आत्म-ज्ञान, विवेक, और अपने वास्तविक स्व की पहचान। कर्मयोग भी उसी सत्य को उपलब्ध करता है, बस रास्ता अलग होता है। इसलिए जो व्यक्ति समझता है कि ज्ञान और कर्म अलग-अलग हैं, वह समझ में कमी रखता है। जो व्यक्ति दोनों को एक ही आत्म-प्राप्ति के दो रूप मानता है, वही सही देखने वाला है। इस श्लोक का आधार है: कर्म को त्यागना ही मुक्ति नहीं है, और कर्म में अटके रहना भी मुक्ति नहीं है; मुक्ति होती है अपनेपन के शून्य होने से।
clearEnglish: This verse states a central teaching of the chapter: the goal reached by the path of discernment is also reached by the path of disciplined action. In other words, what matters is not the external form of the practice but the inner orientation. The Sanskrit words saṅkhya and yoga are not absolute enemies here: saṅkhya points toward knowledge, discrimination, and seeing the Self; yoga points toward action performed with steadiness and non-attachment. Krishna is not saying that every action is equally pure, nor that intellectual insight automatically transforms the person. He is saying that when action is informed by wisdom and when knowledge is lived as a way of being, they converge. The person who sees the one truth behind both is the one who truly sees. This is a correction against false dualism: not “knowledge or action,” but “knowledge in action or action informed by knowledge.”

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse literally says that the state reached by the path of knowledge is also reached by the path of yoga; one who sees both as one sees rightly. It is a statement about convergence, not rivalry.

interpretationPerspectives.label: COMMENTARY
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The DLS summary of this chapter stresses that the final aim is the realization of the Atman, and that the path of Karma Yoga is superior in practice because it purifies the mind while remaining engaged in life. This supports the idea that both paths are not mutually exclusive.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: A practical inference is that one should not live in a false either/or between study and service. Wisdom becomes real when it reduces egoism, and action becomes liberating when it is offered without attachment.

practicalApplication.label: Discernment in action
practicalApplication.text: When you feel pulled between learning and doing, ask: am I trying to escape work, or am I acting from ego? Let one task become an exercise in non-attachment, not performance.

practicalApplication.label: One-pointed attention
practicalApplication.text: Each day, choose one duty and perform it with full attention and a quiet awareness that you are not the doer in the egoic sense.

reflectionQuestion: When do I divide life into 'thinking' and 'doing' instead of seeing them as one path toward inner freedom?
reflectionQuestionHindi: कब मैं जीवन को ‘सोचना’ और ‘करना’ में बाँट देता हूँ, जबकि दोनों को एक ही आत्म-उन्मुखी मार्ग के रूप में देखना चाहिए?
